edits.old: Comparing upgrade performance with different write-concern and journaling settings can confound diagnosis. Percona's 4.4-versus-7.0 write tests and MongoDB's engineering account both identify stronger default durability semantics as a contributor to additional write latency. (high confidence)
edits.new: Comparing upgrade performance with different write-concern settings can confound diagnosis. Percona's write tests on MongoDB 7.0 found the default writeConcern majority had a large impact on write time (127 minutes versus about 10 minutes with writeConcern 1), though Percona also said the performance changes come from multiple code and configuration changes. MongoDB's engineering account says the switch to the default Write Concern Majority improved default durability guarantees but cost performance. Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-performance-regression-benchmarking-and-the-truth-behind-journaling/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/mongodb-8-0-improving-performance-avoiding-regressions

evidence.quote: I tested above with the default writeConcern: majority in v7.0 as I was using a single member only and didn’t consider setting writeConcern:1.
Unfortunately, the performance changes are caused by multiple code and configuration changes.

This change in write concern improved MongoDB’s default durability guarantees but came with a loss in performance since the primary needs to wait for a second write on a second machine to be performed.

edits.old: Successful startup does not rule out application latency regressions. These accounts justify workload-specific testing, not a claim that every upgrade slows queries. (medium confidence)
